svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "A d.c. motor seen from the end: a coil between the poles of a magnet; the field goes from N to S."], [1, "Current flows out of the page on one side of the coil (\u2299) and into the page on the other side (\u2297)."], [2.5, "Fleming\u2019s left-hand rule: the side on the left is pushed up and the side on the right is pushed down. The two forces turn the coil."], [5, "When the coil is vertical, the split-ring commutator reverses the current, so the side now on the left again carries current out of the page."], [8, "The forces always turn the coil the same way: it keeps rotating. More current, a stronger field or more turns make it faster."]]
svg.title: The d.c. motor
svg.desc: End view of a coil rotating between N and S poles: current directions shown with dot and cross symbols, forces up on the left and down on the right, commutator reversing the current each half turn.
svg.text: ⊙ current out of the page · ⊗ current into the page. Rotation: clockwise.

g.data-info: The magnetic field goes from the north pole (N) to the south pole (S).
From N to S across the gap.
Seen end-on. ⊙ = current coming out of the page; ⊗ = current going into the page.
A current-carrying wire in a magnetic field feels a force (the motor effect, F = BIL). Fleming’s left-hand rule: first finger field, second finger current, thumb motion.
Reverses the current in the coil every half turn, when the coil is vertical, so the forces keep turning it the same way.
